_comment: CORRECTIONS to ANSWER KEYS that a question set defines wrongly. Applied by tools/score_answers.py
at scoring time, overriding the key that was copied into each results record when the run was
measured.
This is the third and loudest overlay. The other two move ROUTE, which is a diagnostic; this one
moves CREDIT, which is the headline. A rescore with an entry in here is not the figure published
for that run, and the scorer says so on every invocation where an entry applies.
THE MEASUREMENT IS NEVER TOUCHED. The recorded answer stands exactly as the run produced it, and
only what it is judged against changes. Rescoring is re-judging recorded text, not re-running.
WHY AN OVERLAY AND NOT AN EDIT. A runset is the file a recorded run was measured with, and editing
it makes the recorded figures unreproducible from the thing that produced them. The key is also
copied into every results record at run time, so an edited runset would not reach a rescore anyway.
VERSION-SCOPED, AND IT HAS TO BE. An entry is either a plain string - correct for every run - or an
object keyed by run tag. A tag with no entry in such an object gets NO correction, deliberately,
and the scorer prints which entries it skipped. The reason is that the artefacts a key describes
are regenerated: a count that is true of one artefact set stops being true when the generator
starts covering something it did not cover before. This has happened here - the Blueprint walk
learned to follow macro graphs and to record BindWidget bindings, and call-node counts taken from
the older artefacts are no longer the right answer. Silently judging a new run against an old run's
count is the exact failure this scoping exists to stop.
KEYED BY QUESTION ID, SO IT ONLY MEANS ANYTHING AGAINST THE SET THOSE IDS CAME FROM. Ids are reused
across sets, so an entry carried from one set to another silently replaces an unrelated question's
key - and a wrong answer key is the defect this file exists to repair, not to introduce. Write
entries against the set you are measuring, and do not copy them between sets.
THIS FILE SHIPS EMPTY on purpose, for that reason. The corrections behind the published figures are
described in QUESTION-DEFECTS.md, in prose, where they cannot be applied to the wrong question.
EVERY ENTRY NEEDS A SECTION IN QUESTION-DEFECTS.md saying how the key was wrong, how that was
established, and what rescoring moves. An entry without one is an unexplained change to a score.
SHAPE. One key per question id. The value is either the corrected key string, or an object of
run tag to corrected key string. Keys beginning with an underscore are ignored, so a rationale
lives beside its entry as "_defect": "..." inside the object.
